strategies.name: Naive Sequential Eight All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Performs 8 separate all_reduce dispatches with interleaved local coupling/decoupling transformations between each stage, exactly as shown in the reference implementation. Total of 8 all_reduce dispatches with full W*S payload each time. Maximizes dispatch count but simplest logic; represents the baseline "correct but slow" approach with no optimization.

strategies.name: Fused Local-Op Batched All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Groups the 8 stages into batches where local coupling/decoupling operations are fused into single kernel launches before dispatching all_reduce. Still 8 all_reduce calls but reduces local operation overhead by vectorizing the forward coupling and backward decoupling loops across multiple stages where mathematically valid. Trades register pressure for fewer local-op dispatches.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Replaces each all_reduce with a reduce_scatter (producing S-sized shard per rank) followed by all_gather (broadcasting back to W*S). Each rank only computes coupling on its owned shard between reduce_scatter and all_gather, reducing local arithmetic by W factor per stage. Total 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but smaller intermediate working set and potential for pipelining adjacent RS/AG pairs.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node structure by performing intra-node all_reduce (within each node's devices) followed by inter-node all_reduce on aggregated results, then broadcast back. For 8 stages, this creates 8*(2 intra-node + 1 inter-node + 1 broadcast) = 32 dispatches but each operates on smaller world_size, potentially better utilizing NVLink/local interconnect bandwidth versus cross-node fabric.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapped Communication-Computation
strategies.desc:
Splits the W*S tensor into independent chunks and launches non-blocking all_reduce on chunk[i] while performing coupling/decoupling computation on chunk[i-1]. Requires careful dependency tracking across 8 stages but can overlap network transfer with local arithmetic. Still 8 all_reduce logical operations but uses async dispatch primitives to hide latency; trades code complexity and synchronization overhead for potential wall-clock speedup.
